bounded-context.name: Project registry
bounded-context.purpose: Persist the set of projects the user has registered, expose them over the HTTP API, and safely serve files from any registered project's tree to the Monaco peek drawer. SQLite-backed (`lexicon-viewer.db`); single-process, single-user.
bounded-context.narrative:
Three small jobs done well. The user registers a by absolute path; `POST /api/projects` refuses anything that isn't absolute and pointing at an existing directory (), and the SQLite UNIQUE constraint blocks duplicates () so the registry stays a set. Stored rows carry only what's needed to find the project again later (`id, name, root_path, added_at, last_opened_at`).

term.name: Project
term.definition: A row in the `projects` SQLite table: `{id, name, root_path, added_at, last_opened_at}`. `root_path` is absolute, unique, and must point at an existing directory at register time (re-checked only on register, not on every load). The project's lexicon is read from `<root_path>/lexicon/`.
term.identity-rule: Identity is the SQLite `id` (autoincrement integer). `root_path` is the stable natural key; renaming the project changes `name` but not identity.

term.name: project root
term.definition: The absolute filesystem path the loader and file-serving routes scope their work to. Stored in `Project.root_path`. All path operations (XML walk, file read, future git shell-out) resolve relative to this root and refuse to escape it.
term.equality: By the absolute path string. Two project-roots are interchangeable iff they resolve to the same canonical filesystem path.

term.name: path clamp
term.definition: The safety check applied to every file path requested over `/api/projects/:id/file?path=…`: resolve the requested path against the project root, compute the relative path, and reject if it starts with `..` or is absolute. Prevents `?path=../../etc/passwd`-style escape.
term.returns: The resolved path under the project root, or a `400 path escape` rejection.

invariant.name: rootPath must be absolute and an existing directory
invariant.statement: `POST /api/projects` rejects (`400`) any `rootPath` that is empty, relative, missing, or not a directory.
invariant.rationale: Relative paths are ambiguous (relative to what?) and would silently land in the server's CWD. Refusing them at register time means the stored `root_path` is always safe to feed into `resolve()` and `stat()`.

invariant.name: file-serving rejects path escape
invariant.statement: The `/api/projects/:id/file` route resolves the requested path under the project root and rejects (`400 path escape`) any request whose resolved path is outside the root — i.e. its relative form starts with `..` or is absolute after resolution.
invariant.rationale: Without this clamp, a malicious or accidental `?path=../../something` would serve arbitrary files from the host. The viewer is local-only today, but the path clamp is the real safety check; don't bypass. All future code-anchor opening flows must route through this endpoint.

invariant.name: rootPath is unique across projects
invariant.statement: The `projects.root_path` column has a UNIQUE constraint. Inserting a duplicate raises a SQLite error, which the POST handler surfaces as a `400`.
invariant.rationale: Registering the same directory twice would produce two `Project` rows racing to be "the" project for that path — visible UI duplication and confusing recency. Uniqueness keeps the registry a set, not a multiset.
